event.name: FlagHorizon: Campus Capture the Flag
event.blurb: Follow clues across web security, forensics, cryptography and reverse engineering in a safe sandbox.
event.description:
FlagHorizon is a jeopardy-style capture-the-flag contest where curiosity beats guesswork. Teams explore intentionally vulnerable web applications, inspect suspicious files, untangle small cryptographic puzzles and reverse engineer toy binaries to recover hidden flags. The challenge board starts with beginner routes and branches into harder chains, so a well-coordinated team can divide the work without needing every member to be an expert. All targets belong to an isolated event sandbox; real campus systems are never part of the game.

The six-hour online round includes a briefing on authorized testing and a live support channel for infrastructure issues. Dynamic scoring keeps popular challenges from dominating the table, while optional hints carry a visible points cost. At the finish, leading teams submit short write-ups explaining how they found their flags, then join a review call before prizes are confirmed. Bring a patient approach, clear notes and a willingness to teach teammates what you discover. This is a practical security puzzle day, with strict scope boundaries and space for both first-time solvers and experienced CTF players.

highlights: Four challenge categories with beginner and advanced paths
An isolated, authorized sandbox for every target
Dynamic scoring and transparent hint costs
A finalist write-up discussion focused on reasoning
what_to_expect: Scope and safety briefing before targets unlock
Six hours of collaborative flag hunting
Short solution write-ups and a final review call
eligibility: Students from diploma, undergraduate and postgraduate programmes
Teams of two to four; first-time CTF participants are welcome
prerequisites: Laptop with a terminal and browser
Basic familiarity with HTTP, files and command-line tools
Optional local tools such as Wireshark and a hex editor; no specialist paid software is required
rules: Attack only the explicitly listed challenge hosts and files.
Do not scan campus systems, the registration site or other teams.
Sharing flags, account access or challenge solutions outside your team is prohibited.
Automated denial-of-service, credential stuffing and uncontrolled brute force are prohibited.
Submit three short write-ups for your highest-value solved challenges by 17:00.
Points determine rank; ties go to the earlier final successful flag submission.

prizes.title: FlagHorizon champions
prizes.description: Highest verified team score after write-up and scope review.

faqs.question: Where will the sandbox access details arrive?
faqs.answer: The captain receives the event portal and virtual briefing link by 18:00 IST on 14 November. Challenge credentials unlock after the scope briefing.

faqs.question: Can we participate without Kali Linux?
faqs.answer: Yes. A browser, terminal and freely available inspection tools are enough for the beginner paths; any operating system is acceptable.

faqs.question: How do hints affect our score?
faqs.answer: Each hint displays its points cost before confirmation. Once accepted, that cost is deducted from the challenge score for your team.

faqs.question: What should we do if a challenge host stops responding?
faqs.answer: Post the challenge ID in the private infrastructure support channel. Do not increase scanning traffic; verified outages may receive an announced extension.
